title: Graceful headroom adapter and priority fairing ruleset
author: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight 'soft headroom adapter' that smooths short-term headroom volatility and a new 'priority fairing' ruleset to express tenant-level priority weights that the autoscaler and admission path can use when capacity is constrained. Motivation: production clusters saw frequent micro-spikes that triggered wholesale scale-ups and downstream preemptions; this PR reduces noisy scale events and preserves SLAs for higher-priority tenants while keeping overall utilization high. Changes include: 1) a headroom adapter component that consumes raw cluster signals (free gpu seats, ephemeral reservations, recent preemptions) and emits a decayed headroom estimate per partition; 2) a tenant priority fairing ruleset with config-driven weight tiers and a fallthrough policy (default: weight 1); 3) an admission tweak so low-weight tenants can be gently delayed via soft backpressure rather than immediate eviction when headroom dips; 4) telemetry: new metrics (tenant_util_p50, tenant_util_p95, headroom_smoothed, priority_fairing_denied_count) and debug traces for the adapter decision path; 5) a simulation harness and playback dataset (tests/harness/playbacks) used to validate behavior across 30 synthetic workload traces; 6) a controlled canary gated by a feature flag (enable_priority_fairing) and rollout notes for Dedicated customers. The description below summarizes the intent, testing, and rollback guidance. Intent and scope: this is a runtime and controller-side change affecting Dedicated fleets' autoscaler and admission layers only. It does not change API surface for hosted customers. Testing: unit tests for adapter math, integration tests exercising admission path under synthetic high-concurrency load, and a small-scale cluster canary that was exercised for 48h. Rollback plan: feature flag off, revert config map that populates priority tiers, emergency override to map all tenants to equal weight. See linked Linear tasks for capacity experiments and rollout checklist.

review_comments: Marcus Li: Can you explain the decay constant choice? The PR uses tau=60s; did you sweep greater windows?

Aisha Patel: We did a sweep across [30s, 60s, 180s] in the sim harness; 60s offered best tradeoff on our fleet traces (reduced false scale-ups by ~42% without delaying >1% of high-priority requests). Added a note in headroom_adapter.go and test coverage to validate behavior.
Rhea Singh: The admission tweak looks good but needs a clearer SLA fallback for P0 tenants. If the adapter misestimates headroom, how do we avoid P0 degradation?

Aisha Patel: P0 tenants are pinned to a minimum weight (config override) and win admission until the emergency preemption threshold is reached. I added e2e test and a canary step in the rollout doc that validates P0 latency stays within SLA under simulated outages.
Jordi Alvarez: Telemetry labels look heavy for high-cardinality tenants; can we sample?

Aisha Patel: Telemetry now uses a two-tier approach: emit full per-tenant time series for top-100 tenants by traffic and sampled series for the rest at 1/10th frequency. Documents and metrics_registry contain the sampling knobs.
Marcus Li: LGTM after nits; please squash and re-run CI.
release_notes: Add soft headroom smoothing and tenant priority fairing to reduce noisy autoscaler churn and improve SLA preservation under contention. Rollout behind enable_priority_fairing feature flag for Dedicated fleets.
